title: Interim Processor Risk Waiver and Temporary Access Exhibit
content:
Purpose:
This exhibit defines the operational, technical and evidentiary controls associated with time-limited or emergency access granted to a Processor (or Subprocessor) to Customer data, model weights, or production telemetry. It is intended to be attached to a master DPA or Service Agreement where the Parties anticipate occasional temporary access that cannot be covered by ongoing onboarding documentation (for example: emergent hotfixes on private deployments, short-term incident remediation, or controlled research access).

Scope:
Applies to any third-party agent, contractor, or vendor who is not a continuously approved subprocesser and who will receive credentials or other access methods to production systems, logs, or customer data for a period not exceeding the access window set forth in Section 3.

Key Definitions:
- "Interim Access": Temporary, time-boxed access granted to a Processor for a specific, documented purpose.
- "Evidence Package": The artifacts (logs, screenshots, signed attestations, output samples, deletion receipts) demonstrating what was accessed, actions taken, and how data was handled.
- "Access Owner": Redwood product or infra lead responsible for issuing, supervising, and revoking interim access.

1) Authorization and Purpose Limitation
- Interim Access must be requested via a documented Access Request (template in linked artifacts). Each request must specify the business justification, scope (systems, data classes, model artifacts), minimum privilege needed, and requested duration.
- Access Owner must approve in writing (email or ticket) prior to credentials issuance. Approvals must reference the relevant customer or environment environment id and any required customer approver for private deployments.
- Access is strictly limited to the stated purpose. Any deviation requires a new request and approval.

2) Time-bound Access and Expiry
- Maximum default interim access duration is 72 hours unless an exception is approved by Security and the relevant customer contact. Shorter windows (e.g., 4–24 hours) are preferred.
- All issued credentials must have automated expiration. No permanent credentials may be provided for interim access.

3) Credentialing and Privilege
- Issue ephemeral credentials (short-lived tokens, ephemeral SSH certs, or IAM session tokens) scoped to specific resources and minimum privileges.
- Multi-factor authentication (MFA) is required for console access.
- Credentials must not be embedded in shared documents or chat. Use the approved secrets distribution mechanism.

4) Logging, Monitoring, and Evidence Capture
- All sessions must be logged at the session, command, and file access level where feasible. Access Owner must ensure verbose logging is enabled for the scope of the access.
- The Processor must produce an Evidence Package within 24 hours of access expiry. Minimum required items: session start/stop logs, list of objects accessed, exported output samples (redacted as needed), and a signed attestation of actions taken.
- Evidence retention for interim access artifacts is 180 days unless customer contract requires otherwise.

5) Data Minimization and Handling
- The Processor must access only the minimal dataset required to achieve the authorized purpose. Any exported artifacts must be minimal, redacted, and stored in encrypted containers with access controls.
- Any local copies created for analysis must be encrypted at rest and destroyed with verifiable deletion proof (see Section 7).

6) Encryption and Key Handling
- Data in transit and at rest must be encrypted using company-approved algorithms and key management practices. If the Processor needs a decryption capability, it must be explicitly noted in the Access Request and approved by Security.
- For private deployments where customer-managed keys are used, the Access Owner must coordinate with the customer KMS administrator and document any temporary key access paths.

7) Proof of Deletion and Handback
- Within 48 hours after access expiry, the Processor must provide proof of deletion for any copies or derivatives created during the interim access period. Acceptable proof includes signed deletion receipts, secure shred logs, or KMS key rotation proofs that render copies unrecoverable.
- If the Processor cannot provide mechanical deletion proof (e.g., physical media destroyed by a third-party), a notarized or otherwise attested destruction certificate is required.

8) Incident and Breach Notification
- Any suspected data loss, unauthorized access, or security incident discovered during or after interim access must be reported to Redwood security within 2 hours of detection and to customers per the master agreement timelines.

9) Audit Rights and Forensic Review
- Redwood (and the customer, where contractually permitted) retains the right to audit Processor activity related to interim access. Audits may include remote log reviews and, if necessary, an onsite forensic assessment under supervised conditions. Audits will be scheduled with at least 48-hour notice except in emergency investigations.

10) Indemnity, Liability, and Limitations
- Processor agrees to indemnify Redwood for direct losses arising from the Processor’s gross negligence in the handling of interim access data, subject to the liability caps and carve-outs in the Master Agreement.
- This Exhibit does not alter existing liability protections for either party except to clarify responsibilities specific to interim access.

11) Termination and Revocation Procedures
- Redwood may revoke interim access immediately on discovery of any non-compliance or at customer request. Revocation steps include immediate token invalidation, remote session termination, and an on-demand evidence collection (within the next 8 hours).
- Following revocation, the Processor must provide a post-revocation Evidence Package within 24 hours.

12) Exceptions and Escalations
- Any deviation from the controls in this Exhibit requires a documented exception approved by Security and the legal owner of the master agreement. Escalation path: Access Owner → Security Manager → Head of InfoSec → Legal.

Attachments (required when attaching this Exhibit to a DPA):
- Attachment A: Interim Access Request Template (ticket fields & minimum approvals).
- Attachment B: Evidence Package Checklist (session logs, file access lists, redaction proofs, deletion receipts).
- Attachment C: Sample Session Log Export Format (CSV example).

Operational Notes / Implementation Guidance (non-normative):
- Prefer automated ephemeral access flows (OIDC/SAML with just-in-time role assignment) to manual credential issuance.
- For emergent incident responses, use a 2-step approval (Access Owner + Security Pager) to reduce customer impact while maintaining oversight.
- Keep a rolling 12-month register of all interim accesses including a link to the Evidence Package location and the approving ticket for compliance reviews.

Open questions for negotiation with Customers (examples to include in customer-specific Exhibit):
- Maximum evidence retention period acceptable to the customer.
- Whether customer audit team will participate in interim access audits.
- Approved redaction standards for exported output that contains PII or model prompts.

Signatures:
This Exhibit is accepted by the Parties when executed by authorized signatories of the Master Agreement or when mutually agreed in writing as an amendment to an existing DPA.

-- END EXHIBIT --
